## What this is

An open curriculum for quantitative pharmacology, built in public, aimed at
three audiences: junior scientists in industry, graduate students and postdocs,
and scientists crossing over from adjacent fields.

It exists because the field is not short of teaching material — it is short of
one *path* through the material that a learner can actually run.

## What it is not

It is not a replacement for the community that already exists. The
[ISoP discussion forum](https://discuss.go-isop.org/) is where the field's
practitioner Q&A happens, and it should stay that way. Discussion here attaches
to individual lessons, where the confusion actually occurs.

It is not a certification, and it does not pretend that reading replaces doing.
Every claim it makes about your competence rests on a finished, public analysis.

## Principles

- **Name the decision.** Every lesson opens with the development decision it
  serves. If that cannot be written, the lesson is not ready.
- **Every result runs.** No lesson ships without a notebook that executes in
  continuous integration. Broken code is a build failure, not a footnote.
- **Show the failure mode.** Each lesson breaks something on purpose and shows
  the diagnostic that catches it. This is the part that experience buys.
- **Truth is published.** Case data are simulated from documented models, so
  every exercise can be graded.
- **Open tools by default.** Concepts are taught on software anyone can install.
  Proprietary tools are referenced, never redistributed.

## Licence

Content is **CC BY-SA 4.0** — reuse it in your teaching, keep derivatives open.
Code and data-generation scripts are **MIT**.

## Contributing

Corrections, better explanations and new lessons are all welcome. See
`CONTRIBUTING.md` in the repository. The most useful contribution is usually the
least glamorous: telling us exactly where you got stuck.

## Disclaimer

Educational material. The compounds are fictional, the models are illustrative,
and nothing here is clinical guidance or a regulatory position.
